title: Use a four-vertex path to refute direct negative association of matching edge indicators
statement: For the four-vertex path with edges e1,e2,e3 and fixed lambda>0, Z=1+3lambda+lambda^2, Pr(e1,e3 in M)=lambda^2/Z and Pr(e1 in M)=(lambda+lambda^2)/Z. Therefore Cov(X_e1,X_e3)=lambda^3/Z^2>0. Arbitrary matching EDGE-indicator laws cannot be directly identified with negatively associated or strongly Rayleigh laws, and a standard DPP sampler cannot simply be applied to that representation. This does not exclude a different auxiliary representation or a full parallel sampler.
